# requestrepo

> requestrepo captures HTTP requests, DNS queries and SMTP mail sent to a throwaway subdomain of {{DOMAIN}}, and lets you script the HTTP responses and DNS records that subdomain serves. Everything is available over a plain JSON REST API, so an agent can use it with curl alone: no SDK, no MCP server, no browser.

Typical uses: testing webhooks and integrations, inspecting exactly what a client or server sends, checking that an email or DNS lookup actually happens, and serving a custom response or DNS record during development or an authorized security assessment.

The whole loop is three calls. Create a session, point something at its domain, then read what arrived:

```sh
S=$(curl -s -X POST {{ORIGIN}}/api/v2/sessions)
TOKEN=$(jq -r .token <<<"$S"); URL=$(jq -r .url <<<"$S")
curl -s "${URL}hello?x=1"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "{{ORIGIN}}/api/v2/requests?last=20&view=summary" | jq -c '.requests[]'
```

To wait for a callback instead of checking for one, use `requests?after=now&wait=60&view=summary`, started before you trigger it; pass the returned `cursor` as `after` to wait for the next one.

## Docs

- [Agent guide and API reference]({{ORIGIN}}/docs/api.md): Sessions, reading captured traffic (cursor and long polling), custom responses, DNS records, sharing, errors. Start here.
- [OpenAPI description]({{ORIGIN}}/openapi.json): Machine-readable description of every endpoint.
- [Agent Skill]({{ORIGIN}}/skill.md): A SKILL.md for Claude Code, Codex and other agents that load skills. Save it as `requestrepo/SKILL.md` in your skills directory.

## Abuse

- [Reporting abuse]({{ORIGIN}}/docs/abuse.md): How to report a subdomain used for malware, phishing or other abuse, over the API or at {{ORIGIN}}/abuse.

## Optional

- [API catalog]({{ORIGIN}}/.well-known/api-catalog): RFC 9727 linkset pointing at the API description and docs.
- [Source code](https://github.com/adrgs/requestrepo): requestrepo is open source and self-hostable.
